buyer_reported_costs.finding: An agency operator running client voice agents on Retell reports an average of about $0.17 per minute year-to-date across a mix of simple and complex agents, 'JUST the retellai cost' - i.e. excluding separate middleware/API spend.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Retell community support thread, June 2026; practitioner reply, not a Retell statement

buyer_reported_costs.finding: Other practitioners in the same thread report roughly 11-15 cents/min for simple agents, 16-23 cents/min for complex ones, $0.12-$0.14/min typical for their clients, and $0.35-$0.40/min for a high-quality ElevenLabs v3 voice with 6k+ token knowledge base.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Same Retell community thread, June 2026; community-reported ranges, not verified invoices

buyer_reported_costs.finding: A customer running 1,044 outbound calls (567 answered, ~22 min 10 s of call duration in the export) was billed about $32.69, which they calculated as about $1.47 per effective minute against an advertised ~$0.12/min.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Retell community billing-dispute post, May 2026; the poster's own arithmetic on their invoice, disputed with the vendor - reported, not verified

buyer_reported_costs.finding: A 229-second call cost $0.7391 and a 173-second call cost $0.6358 on a ~13.6¢/min headline rate - roughly 5x - because of an LLM token surcharge applied when average input tokens per request exceeded 3,500.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Retell community thread, April 2026; the per-call breakdown was posted by Retell support, so these are vendor-confirmed invoice line items

buyer_reported_costs.finding: Retell's own support answer in that thread lists a real 229-second call as voice engine $0.210 + platform TTS $0.057 + GPT-5.1 $0.153 + US Twilio telephony $0.057 + LLM token surcharge $0.262.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Same thread; shows the four-part cost stack and the size of the surcharge relative to the advertised rate

buyer_reported_costs.finding: Vendors' own comparison figures: Bland states that adding typical provider rates brings most production Vapi stacks to roughly $0.13 to $0.30/min and Retell to $0.11 to $0.25/min, while Telnyx states Vapi realistic all-in is $0.12-$0.42/min and Retell $0.088-$0.31/min, and its own ≈$0.06/min.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Competitor marketing claims published on vendor pricing pages (Bland FAQ, Telnyx comparison table dated July/Aug 2026); treat as third-party claims, not verified invoices

buyer_reported_costs.finding: Goodcall claims a live human answering service runs about $1.50 to $1.90 a minute, versus about 13¢/min for its Starter plan at four-minute calls.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Vendor claim on Goodcall's pricing FAQ, used only as a marker for the human-answering-service alternative; not independently verified

what_is_included_vs_extra.point: Builder platforms price the parts, not the whole: Retell's headline $0.07-$0.31/min is the sum of voice engine $0.055 + TTS $0.015-$0.10 + LLM $0.006-$0.38 + telephony $0.015, so the model and voice choice swing the total by roughly 5x.

Retell meters capability as per-minute deltas: knowledge base +$0.005/min, denoising +$0.005/min, guardrails +$0.005/min, PII removal +$0.01/min, branded outbound +$0.10/call, AI QA $0.10/min - the 'extras' an integrator normally configures.
Vapi passes model costs through at cost with no markup and charges the $0.05/min hosting fee on top; HIPAA-eligible handling is a $2,000/month add-on, and extra concurrency is $10/line/month.

Vapi's own documentation says audio is transcribed on both channels (caller and assistant), voice is billed per character spoken, and long calls get more expensive because growing conversation history is re-sent with each request.

Bland bundles LLM, STT and TTS into one per-minute rate with no token charges, but keeps telephony separate (own carrier or Bland's Twilio at pass-through); warm/live transfers, SMS nodes, appointment-scheduling node and guardrails are Enterprise-only.

ElevenLabs adds no telephony fee of its own - calls bill at the same call-minute rate as any other channel - but the buyer must connect Twilio or a SIP trunk and pay that carrier directly, and LLM usage is billed separately.
ElevenLabs burst pricing doubles the rate to $0.160/min when a workspace exceeds its plan concurrency, and downgrading forfeits unused paid credits.

Deepgram's Voice Agent rate bundles STT + a managed LLM + TTS, and the price drops from $0.075 to $0.050/min if the buyer brings their own LLM and TTS - a direct measure of what the orchestration layer is worth.

Telnyx includes HIPAA readiness and 500 concurrent calls on pay-as-you-go, but rounds each call's connected duration up to the next full minute - which it itself warns inflates cost 'especially for short calls'.

At the managed-receptionist end, what the monthly fee buys is the integration work: calendar booking, warm transfers, after-hours flows and human handoff are gated to higher tiers (Vocenya Growth/Pro), and human backup is a separately quoted per-call rate.
Synthflow no longer publishes a per-minute rate at all: integrations, telephony, security review and launch engineering are scoped into one annual enterprise contract, with no free plan or trial.

buyer_complaints.complaint: Billing opacity on the cheap per-minute model: a multi-agent operator could not reconcile exported call durations with invoices, could not separate telephony/SIP/LLM/STT/TTS costs, and did not know whether silence, voicemail or connection time was billable - and calculated an effective $1.47/min against an advertised $0.12/min.

Hidden token surcharge: exceeding ~3,500 average input tokens per LLM request silently multiplied billed LLM duration, turning a 13.6¢/min headline into 76¢ for a sub-4-minute call, and the user asked for (and was told there is no) alert for the threshold.

Price unpredictability is the recurring theme: the headline per-minute rate omits telephony, model choice, prompt size and per-call minimums, so the same agent can cost 5-10x its advertised rate once prompts grow.
Synthflow's move to enterprise-only pricing with no trial or per-minute rate removes the low-risk entry point smaller buyers need before committing.

price_ranges.low_cost_self_serve: $0.05-$0.16 per connected minute at list (platform/voice-engine $0.05-$0.08 + model + STT $0.005-$0.017 + telephony $0.002-$0.015), or $29-$99/month for a self-serve account with included minutes
price_ranges.mid_market: $0.10-$0.20 per minute realistically all-in for a working agent, plus $79-$499/month for packaged SMB plans with bundled minutes
price_ranges.full_service_or_custom: $280-$700/month plus $199-$3,000 one-time setup for a managed deployment; $2,000-$5,000/month minimum spend or custom annual contracts at enterprise tier
price_ranges.inference_note: Per-minute ranges are assembled from list prices on each vendor's own rate card: cheapest credible stack = Deepgram/Telnyx STT ~$0.005 + cheap LLM ~$0.006-$0.02 + TTS ~$0.015 + Telnyx telephony ~$0.0032 + a $0.05 voice engine, floor around $0.08-$0.10 (Telnyx itself states ~$0.06 for its bundled stack, and Retell's component floor computes below its $0.07 headline). The top of the range uses premium voices (ElevenLabs v3 at $0.10/min on Retell) and frontier models ($0.16-$0.38/min). Monthly ranges are the published subscription tiers of Goodcall, ElevenLabs, Vocenya and Rosie-style SMB services; setup figures come from Voicewell ($199-$499) and the search-reported NJ figures, which is why the full-service setup band is wide. No range here is a vendor's own 'all-in' quote except where explicitly labelled.

implications_for_consultancy: Inference: the consultancy is not selling minutes, it is selling the $0.05-$0.15/min of engineering that decides whether a buyer lands at $0.10/min or $0.40/min. Retell's own rate card shows the same agent can cost 5x more purely from voice and model choice, and a 3,500-token prompt threshold can silently 5x a call (see complaints). Pricing the engagement around that arbitrage - picking the cheap voice/model, trimming the prompt - is defensible and is measurable against the buyer's actual invoices.

Inference: an all-in platform cost of $0.10-$0.20/min means 1,000 minutes/month is only $100-$200 of vendor spend. A $500-$900/month managed retainer therefore looks expensive against the raw bill unless it is framed as replacing a receptionist or answering service, not replacing a subscription. Buyers already accept $350-$499/month for nothing more than an AI receptionist (Sarah247, Vocenya Pro), and $280-$380/month plus $199-$299 setup for managed setups (Voicewell); that is the anchor to price against.

Inference: NJ/tri-state published prices cluster at $49-$99/month entry, $249-$350/month mid, $499-$697/month high, with setup from $0-$2,997. A local consultancy can credibly sit at a $1,500-$3,000 one-time build plus $300-$600/month including hosting and tuning, because that undercuts the $2,997 + $697/month NJ outlier while sitting above the $49/month self-serve tools the buyer could sign up for unaided - and the gap is justified by integration, number porting, tuning and a local human to call.

Inference: the $49-$99/month self-serve plans (Vocenya Value, Goodcall Starter, ElevenLabs Starter) define the floor of what a buyer will pay for software, but they cap included minutes at 100-300 and bill $0.25-$0.35/min past that, so a 1,000-minute business pays $200-$300/month anyway. Quoting a flat monthly fee with a stated minute allowance (and a clear overage at or below $0.25/min) matches how this market already prices and avoids the complaint pattern about unexplained surcharges.

Inference: setup fee is expected in the managed segment, not the self-serve one - Voicewell charges $199/$299/$499 one-time, Sarah247 bundles setup in, and NJ providers publish up to $2,997. Charging a visible setup fee signals 'done for you' and funds the build; hiding the build cost inside monthly fees makes the monthly number look uncompetitive against $49/month software.

Inference: the strongest defensible premium is auditability and aftercare. The loudest buyer complaints are billing opacity and surprise surcharges, and Telnyx's own footnote admits 60-second per-call rounding inflates short-call costs. A monthly package that includes a call-cost breakdown, a hard cap on overage, prompt-size hygiene and quarterly tuning answers the exact failure buyers report, so a higher monthly fee is defensible on that basis rather than on minutes.

Inference: avoid quoting per-minute all-in prices the consultancy cannot control. Platform rate cards changed materially in 2026 (Retell added a token surcharge, Synthflow went enterprise-only with no trial, ElevenLabs introduced burst pricing). A pilot priced as a fixed build plus a fixed monthly service fee, with platform pass-through shown separately at cost, protects margin when the vendor changes its rate card mid-engagement.

Inference: for clients with heavy call volume or complex integrations, the honest comparison is not Goodcall at $79/month but Synthflow/Vapi Pro-class contracts at $999-$2,000/month minimums. Those buyers expect a named human and an SLA, which is where a local consultancy with a monthly retainer in the low four figures is priced correctly rather than overpriced.
caveats: Twilio's voice pricing page is script-rendered and returned no prices on direct fetch; the $0.014/$0.0085/$0.022 and $1.15/$2.15 figures came from the search engine's rendering of that URL and are corroborated by Telnyx's published competitor table (Twilio $0.014 out / $0.0085 in, Aug 2026). Retell's LLM price list is a long live table (GPT 5.x/6.x, Claude 5.x, Gemini 3.x/4) and is a snapshot as of retrieval; model names and rates change frequently.
Buyer-reported per-minute figures come from vendor-run community forums and one invoice dispute; they are self-reported and not audited.
Monthly per-minute-equivalent comparisons (e.g. Rosie at $49 for 250 minutes) are arithmetic on the vendor's own list price, not a vendor-stated rate.

Search-engine summaries were used to locate NJ providers; Vocenya and Sarah247 were opened and read directly, but the NJ figures attributed to NJ Business AI ($697/month + $2,997 setup) and WebFront AI were only seen in search summaries and their pages could not be opened (404 on the cited URL), so they are deliberately excluded from offerings.
data_gaps: Synthflow publishes no price of any kind after moving to enterprise-only annual contracts; no per-minute or setup figure exists to cite.
No vendor publishes a single audited 'all-in per minute' including telephony for a realistic SMB agent; the closest are Telnyx's ~$0.06 (self-interested) and buyers' $0.11-$0.40 reports.
Retell and Vapi both have interactive calculators whose outputs are not in the page text; their calculated all-in numbers could not be captured for a stated call profile.
Typical monthly minute volumes for 5-200 staff businesses in Middlesex County were not sourced, so monthly spend ranges rest on the vendors' own bundled allowances (75-3,738 minutes).
Reddit threads on per-minute costs (r/vapiai, r/AIReceptionists, r/VoiceAutomationAI) appeared in search results but were not opened, so their figures are not cited here.
Twilio's phone-number pricing page did not render; the $1.15 local / $2.15 toll-free monthly figures are from the search rendering of the voice pricing URL and should be re-verified.
No New Jersey or tri-state vendor was found publishing a pure per-minute builder rate (as opposed to a managed monthly plan); NJ pricing in this file is all managed-receptionist pricing.
